Subject: SOC2 SIG request — vulnerability mgmt clarification

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this. FinEdge's external audit team has a couple of follow-ups on the vulnerability management section of the SIG/C A I Q that we'd like clarified before our scheduled review next week. Specifically they asked for: 

- A concise statement of scan cadence (authenticated vs unauthenticated), scheduling windows, and tooling used.
- The SLA for CVE remediation by severity (our audit team wants to see measurable windows and escalation flow).
- Evidence that shows sample CVE ticketing exports (last 90 days) and a mapping to the remediation timeline.
- Confirmation of scan/log retention for at least 12 months.

Can you provide those items (or point me to the exact docs) by EOD Friday 10/23? If you can attach a scan matrix and a short attestation, that would be ideal.

Best,
Lydia
Compliance Manager, FinEdge

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear list. We can get this over to you. Quick notes / plan: 

- Scan cadence: weekly unauthenticated perimeter scans; credentialed (authenticated) scans run every 30 days for platform services and every 14 days for customer-facing endpoints. We’ll include the tooling names in the matrix (Nessus for credentialed, OpenVAS for network, and an internal agent for continuous container checks).
- SLA by severity: proposed doc below — Critical (exploitability high): 7 calendar days to mitigation + 24h incident escalation; High: 14 days; Medium: 45 days; Low: 90 days. We’ll attach a remediation_timeline PDF that maps examples to those windows.
- Evidence: we will attach a CSV export of CVE tickets (filtered last 90 days) and a scan_matrix CSV with timestamps.
- Retention: scan logs retained 18 months (raw logs), normalized scan index retained 36 months for audit snapshots.

We will assemble: scan_matrix_2026Q3.csv, remediation_timeline_20261021.pdf, cve_sample_export_20261020.csv.

If you want a signed attestation, we can produce a short letter and have it signed; that will be ready early Friday (10/23).

If that works we’ll upload to the Drive link and send DocuSign for the attestation.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Security Engagement Lead, Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.com

Subject: Internal: VM evidence & timeline (draft)

Jasmine / Ben — drafting the pieces Lydia requested. Technical details for the matrix: 

- Scanners & cadence:
  * Nessus (credentialed) — monthly for infra services, bi-weekly for customer infra; authenticated profiles include playbook checks and exploitability scoring.
  * OpenVAS (external edge) — weekly unauthenticated sweeps.
  * Agent-based container checks (internal) — continuous; daily baseline alerts for new CVE appearances.

- CVE triage + SLA workflow:
  1) Auto-detection -> triage queue (SRE) within 4 hours of detection for critical signatures.
  2) Initial assessment and owner assigned inside 24 hours.
  3) Patch/mitigation plan in 72 hours for criticals; deployment window target 7 days (exceptions require documented approval chain).
  4) Post-deploy validation and closure ticket with evidence of patch, scan re-run, and baseline comparison.

- Retention specifics: raw scan outputs (S3) retained 18 months, normalized index (Elastic) retained 36 months, exported artifacts snapshots (zip) kept for SOC2 bundles for 5 years upon request.

I’ve attached a draft remediation timeline and a sample CVE export (redacted). Small ask for sales: Ben, if FinEdge needs an expedited attestation signature we should clear via Sales so we can prioritize the legal sign-off.

Attachment: remediation_timeline_20261021.pdf; cve_sample_export_20261020.csv

—Irene

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@finedge.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-23T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 SIG request — vulnerability mgmt clarification

Lydia — quick clarifications (to be reflected verbatim in the attestation):

- Start-point for SLA: the 7-day Critical SLA is measured from detection timestamp (automated or manual) when the CVE is classified as exploitable in our triage. If exploitability is confirmed later, the remediation timeline is driven from the detection + confirmation milestone but the initial detection must be logged to the ticket.

- Maintenance/blackout windows: we maintain scheduled maintenance windows (typically Sundays 01:00–05:00 UTC) for high-impact changes that can affect scan runs. Missed authenticated scans due to maintenance are documented in the scan matrix and a re-run is scheduled within 48 hours post-window; if a re-run is not possible within 48 hours we escalate and document compensating controls (e.g., manual verification) — these compensating actions are included in the remediation ticket and in the scan_matrix_2026Q3.csv column: "re-run_or_compensating_control_notes".

I’ve uploaded the following to the Drive link and attached signed-vm-attestation-20261023.pdf via DocuSign: scan_matrix_2026Q3.csv; remediation_timeline_20261021.pdf; cve_sample_export_20261020.csv; signed-vm-attestation-20261023.pdf.

Let me know if you want a short call to walk through.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Security Engagement Lead, Redwood Inference
